validity.recommendation: Treat as a dropped 2021 route option; shelve (Presumed) or merge the concept into the pursued onshore P3620/P7864 family. No offshore subsea line was ever advanced.
validity.researcher_notes: The row records a real 2021 PROPOSAL, not a hallucination: in Feb–Oct 2021 Israel discussed an OFFSHORE/subsea pipeline running directly from the Leviathan rig to Egypt's LNG terminals. Independently confirmed by Times of Israel ('offshore rig direct to Egypt'), Enerdata (Mar 2021, describes 'a subsea pipeline project' from Leviathan, ~10 bcm/y), and World Oil (Feb 2021). HOWEVER this was one of two competing ROUTE OPTIONS floated in 2021 (offshore subsea vs an onshore route). The route that was actually pursued is the ONSHORE one: government-approved 2023, $610m INGL EPC signed June 2025 for a 65 km Ramat Hovav→Nitzana line, completion 2028 (Times of Israel, Enerdata). I found NO independent evidence post-2021 that a distinct offshore/subsea Israel–Egypt pipeline advanced—every 2023–2025 development names the onshore Nitzana route. So the offshore entity is an abandoned/superseded alternative alignment. Existence-as-a-live-project is doubtful even though the 2021 proposal was genuine.

validity.recommendation: Reconcile with P3620 (Israel–Egypt Onshore Gas Pipeline) and the P7864 Nitzana row — same 2021 origin, same objective, same owner (INGL); P3657 is the offshore variant of that project family.
validity.researcher_notes: P3620 'Israel–Egypt Onshore Gas Pipeline' is the sibling row: both were created from the same Oct-2021 Reuters/Times of Israel reporting about 'a new pipeline to boost gas exports to Egypt', both proposed 2021, both owner Israel Natural Gas Lines, same source fields, same Israel→Egypt corridor. They are the two route options for one project. Because the onshore option (now P3620, physically the 65 km Ramat Hovav→Nitzana line = P7864 'Nitzana Pipeline') is the one advancing, P3657 double-counts the same export objective under an offshore label that was not built. Not literally the same physical pipe, but a dropped-alternative duplicate of the P3620 family — recommend consolidating rather than carrying as an independent live project.

validity.recommendation: Do not treat Capacity=6.70 bcm/y as this pipeline's design capacity — it is an aggregate export-volume figure; leave blank or requalify.
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity 6.70 bcm/y does not describe a distinct offshore pipeline. 6.7 bcm/y is the PHASE-1 total Leviathan→Egypt supply volume under the Aug-2025 $35bn export deal (raising current supply from 4.7 to 6.7 bcm/y), delivered via the existing EMG/Arish–Ashkelon route plus the new onshore Nitzana line — not a single offshore pipe's throughput. The 2021 offshore proposal itself was quoted around ~10 bcm/y (Enerdata Mar 2021). The onshore Nitzana line is spec'd at 600 mmcf/d (~6.2 bcm/y). So the 6.70 figure is an anachronistic, aggregate number mis-assigned to this offshore row.

Leviathan is firmly the source field for the direct offshore-rig proposal (both sources). Tamar is associated with Israel–Egypt export volumes generally but is less clearly the feed for THIS offshore concept — hence medium, caveat on the 'Tamar' portion.

Left UNRESOLVED / not corroborated. 6.70 bcm/y is not a verified capacity of an offshore pipeline — it matches the phase-1 aggregate Leviathan→Egypt supply volume under the Aug-2025 export deal, not a single-pipe design figure. See spec concern. Not filling a paired ref for a value that does not describe this entity.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Proposed since 2021 (Enerdata Mar 2021, Times of Israel Oct 2021). No independent news at any point 2022–2026 that a DISTINCT offshore/subsea Israel–Egypt pipeline advanced. Every subsequent development concerns the ONSHORE route instead: Israeli government approval 2023, $610m INGL EPC for the 65 km Ramat Hovav→Nitzana line signed June 2025 (Times of Israel), completion 2028 (Enerdata), and the Aug-2025 $35bn Leviathan–Egypt export deal delivered via existing EMG + the onshore Nitzana line. The offshore option was effectively superseded and is dormant >2 years. Applying the proposed>=2y->shelved dormancy rule with ShelvedCancelledType=Presumed. Per standing rule 2 the presumed inference carries no fabricated ref; last offshore-specific evidence date is 2021-10. Alternatively, cancel/merge into the onshore P3620/P7864 family (see duplicate concern).

summary: P3657 is a genuine 2021 offshore proposal but a superseded/duplicate alternative of the pursued onshore P3620/P7864 Nitzana route; no post-2021 offshore progress, capacity 6.7bcm is a mis-assigned aggregate figure — stage shelved (Presumed).
